description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic featuring tender chicken pieces swimming in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. This iconic dish balances sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors, making it a comforting and incredibly satisfying meal. Perfect for a special lunch or dinner, its vibrant color and aromatic spices will transport your taste buds straight to India.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Mix everything thoroughly to coat the chicken. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or unsalted butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, making sure not to overcrowd the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side until the chicken is lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set it aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ghee or unsalted butter. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté over medium heat until it becomes translucent and lightly golden, which should take about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Makhani Flavor
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, drained soaked cashews, Kashmiri red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, sugar, and salt to taste to the pan. Mix all the ingredients well. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly and the oil begins to separate from the mixture.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce to Smoothness
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until the sauce is completely smooth and creamy. If necessary, add a small splash of water to help achieve the desired consistency. For an extra luxurious texture, you may pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish the Curry
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken pieces to the smooth sauce in the pan. Stir in the crushed fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) and the heavy cream. Simmer the butter chicken gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing all the flavors to fully meld together and the chicken to heat through. Avoid bringing the sauce to a rolling boil after adding the cream.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Ladle the hot Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and an extra swirl of heavy cream, if desired, for a beautiful presentation. Serve immediately with warm naan bread, fluffy basmati rice, or roti.

tips: For an authentic smoky flavor, you can char the cooked chicken slightly on a grill or under a broiler before adding it to the sauce.
Soaking cashews is crucial for achieving a smooth and creamy sauce without adding too much heavy cream. Almonds can be a substitute if cashews are unavailable.
Store leftover Butter Chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It often tastes even better the next day as the flavors deepen.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Guide to a Creamy Indian Lunch Recipe

Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani, is more than just a dish; it's a culinary embrace. A symphony of tender chicken pieces luxuriating in a rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato gravy, it has captivated palates worldwide. Perfect for a hearty lunch, a comforting dinner, or even a special occasion, this iconic Indian creation promises a delightful experience with every bite. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality flavor in your own kitchen, you've come to the right place. This guide will walk you through the history, ingredients, and step-by-step process to master this beloved Indian lunch staple.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

The origins of Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s. Legend has it that Kundan Lal Gujral, the founder, experimented with leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream. The result was an instant sensation, giving birth to one of the most famous Indian dishes globally. "Murgh" translates to chicken, and "Makhani" means buttery, perfectly describing the essence of this dish.

What makes Butter Chicken so universally adored? It’s the perfect balance of flavors. The chicken, often marinated in yogurt and spices, is succulent and tender. The gravy, a velvety concoction of pureed tomatoes, cashews (for richness), butter, and cream, is subtly sweet, tangy, and infused with aromatic spices like cardamom, cinnamon, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). It’s not overly spicy, making it appealing to a wide range of palates, and its luxurious texture makes it an incredibly satisfying choice for an Indian lunch.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Murgh Makhani

To embark on your Butter Chicken journey, gathering the right ingredients is key. Quality makes a significant difference in the final taste.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken (thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces)
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste

**For the Creamy Gravy:**
*   2 tbsp butter (plus more for cooking chicken)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 medium fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, then drained)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1/2 tsp red chili powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp ground coriander
*   1/4 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or cashew cream for a dairy-free option)
*   1 tsp sugar (optional, to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

**Whole Spices (Optional, but recommended for depth):**
*   2-3 green cardamom pods
*   1 small cinnamon stick
*   2-3 cloves
*   1 bay leaf

## Step-by-Step Butter Chicken Instructions

Now, let's dive into making your perfect Butter Chicken. Patience and attention to detail will yield the best results.

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken (Minimum 30 minutes, ideally 2-4 hours or overnight)**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate.

**Step 2: Cook the Marinated Chicken**
Heat 1-2 tablespoons of butter or oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Gravy Base**
In the same pan, add another tablespoon of butter. If using whole spices, add them now and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until aromatic.

**Step 4: Build the Gravy Flavors**
Add the pureed tomatoes (or crushed tomatoes), soaked cashews, red chili powder, garam masala, ground coriander, and turmeric powder. Stir well. Add 1/2 cup of water or broth. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the mixture is thick.

**Step 5: Blend for Smoothness**
Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender (remove whole spices if you used them). Blend until completely smooth and creamy. This step is crucial for achieving that signature velvety texture. You may need to add a splash more water if the mixture is too thick to blend.

**Step 6: Finish the Butter Chicken Gravy**
Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Stir in the remaining butter, heavy cream, and crushed kasoori methi. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy. Season with sugar (if using) and salt to taste. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich gravy.

**Step 7: Garnish and Serve**
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Your homemade Butter Chicken is now ready to be enjoyed!

## Pro Tips for the Best Creamy Butter Chicken

To elevate your homemade Butter Chicken from good to extraordinary, consider these pro tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Don't Skip Blending:** A smooth, lump-free gravy is a hallmark of authentic Murgh Makhani. Use a high-speed blender or immersion blender for the best results.
*   **Kasoori Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) lend a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is indispensable for authentic Butter Chicken. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their oils.
*   **Balance Sweetness and Acidity:** Tomatoes can vary in acidity. A pinch of sugar helps balance the flavors and achieve that perfect mild sweetness.
*   **Use Good Quality Ingredients:** Fresh tomatoes, good butter, and rich cream make a noticeable difference.
*   **Resting Time:** Like many stews and curries, Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. It's a fantastic dish for meal prepping your Indian lunch!

## Serving Suggestions for Indian Butter Chicken

Whether you're enjoying Butter Chicken for a special occasion or a quick weekday lunch, the right accompaniments complete the meal.

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, chewy naan bread is perhaps the most classic pairing. Its ability to soak up the rich gravy is unmatched. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delicious.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Fluffy basmati rice or aromatic jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a neutral base that perfectly complements the rich curry.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Other Indian breads like whole wheat roti or flaky paratha are also excellent choices.
*   **Side Salad or Raita:** A simple cucumber and onion salad or a cooling cucumber raita (yogurt dip) can cut through the richness of the Butter Chicken, offering a refreshing contrast.
*   **Pickles:** A small side of Indian lime or mango pickle can add a tangy, spicy kick for those who enjoy it.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is undeniably delicious, there are several ways to adapt it to dietary preferences or availability of ingredients.

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Easily transform this into Paneer Makhani by replacing chicken with cubed paneer (Indian cottage cheese). Tofu or mixed vegetables (like peas, carrots, and potatoes) also work wonderfully.
*   **Vegan Version:** For a vegan option, use plant-based butter, coconut milk or cashew cream instead of dairy cream, and omit the yogurt from the marinade (use a plant-based yogurt or lemon juice). Replace chicken with chickpeas, firm tofu, or a mix of vegetables.
*   **Healthier Option:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or opt for low-fat cream. Use lean chicken breast. You can also increase the vegetable content by adding finely diced carrots or bell peppers to the gravy base.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For a milder curry, use less or stick to Kashmiri chili powder, which primarily provides color. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Cooking Method for Chicken:** While pan-frying is common, grilling the marinated chicken (like tandoori chicken) before adding it to the gravy imparts a lovely smoky flavor.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a testament to the magic of Indian cuisine – a dish that’s comforting, luxurious, and bursting with flavor. With this comprehensive guide, you have everything you need to prepare a truly exceptional Butter Chicken that will impress your family and friends, making any lunch feel like a special occasion. So, next time you're craving a rich, comforting, and utterly satisfying Indian meal, remember the magic of Butter Chicken. Happy cooking!
